correctness.rationale: Proof partitions all self-inverse partial isometries by hub absent, hub fixed, or exchanged with a rim vertex; each case is disjoint and exhaustive. Wheel diameter two reduces rim involutions to automorphisms of induced paths; a direct cyclic run count and explicit wreath-product involution count prove the partition formula. Hub exchange forces all remaining domain elements to the two rim neighbors and yields n(z^2+2z^3+2z^4). An independent metric-based exhaustive enumeration agrees at each rank for 3<=n<=9; these finite tests supplement, not replace, the general proof.

originality.rationale: The full wheel-monoid source (Fernandes, arXiv:2307.16257v2) was examined in the parts defining the metric, the exceptional hub maps and the rank/Green structural theorems; no involution-rank polynomial is stated. A general partial-graph-automorphism source (Jajcay et al., arXiv:1809.04422v2) provides structural characterization rather than these coefficients. The related cycle-metric dihedral-restriction count does not imply the wheel rim component counts because wheel distances between nonadjacent rim vertices are two and hub-exchanging involutions are additional. Actual published-literature searches under the listed terms disclosed no equivalent formula. Residual unindexed-literature risk remains.

value.rationale: Determines all coefficients of a natural full-monoid rank invariant for every finite wheel with at least five rim vertices, not an arbitrary computational slice. The explicit parity term, cyclic-path-component involution products and sharply rank-bounded hub-exchange correction distinguish this invariant from known group-unit counts and rank/Green classifications. The result gives a reusable classification technique for involutions in related graph partial-isometry monoids.
